In a sealed-bid, second-price auction, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true private value. This is because:

1. If you bid less than your true value, you might miss out on winning when you should (you could have won at a price you're willing to pay)
2. If you bid more than your true value, you might overpay if you win, which would be irrational

Since your private value is $80, bidding exactly $80 is weakly dominant - it's always at least as good as any other bid, and it's optimal when others also bid truthfully.
